newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends lower in line with fall in JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends lower in line with fall in JGBs.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures ended lower on Tuesday due to a fall in Japanese government bonds and a rise in Tokyo share prices.
"A fall in JGB futures late in the afternoon, and a recovery in share prices to above 18,000 points led to selling of euroyen futures," a city bank trader said.
The yen's weakness against the dollar on Tuesday had little effect on euroyen futures, traders said.

"The dollar's rise has been spurred by expectations that the spread between U.S. and Japanese interest rates will increase from here. Movement in (Japanese) interest rates is the cause, and not the effect, of currency fluctuations," a trader for another city bank said.

The mood in the euroyen futures market was dampened on Tuesday morning on news that Kabun Muto, director-general of the Management and Coordination Agency, had urged the Bank of Japan to consider the possibility of raising the official discount rate (ODR), traders said.

Asked if Muto made any reference to a possible rise in the ODR at this morning's economic ministers' meeting, the spokesman quoted Muto as saying: "I asked (the BOJ's Yasuo Matsushita) to consider the possibility."
Muto said that growth in Japan's money supply has been slow and this can be explained by the outflow of Japanese funds into higher yielding assets overseas, the spokesman said.

Traders said the impact from Muto's comments was limited, however, as BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita has repeatedly said that Japan's monetary policy emphasises strengthening the basis for Japan's economic recovery.
